title: SAARTHI answer
description: Contract 3. Frozen. Owner: Builder 1. Consumed by the agent prompt, validate_answer, the Streamlit UI and the eval harness. Source: COPILOT-SPEC.md 2 and ARCHITECTURE-HANDOFF.md Contract 3. SPEC.md 7 shows an older flat evidence_ids form; that example is stale.

classification.description: Set by classify_question BEFORE any retrieval. CLASS_A never reaches the agent.

overall_status.description: partial names a missing capability in limitations. refused is CLASS_A only.

known_as_of.description: R2. TIMESTAMP_NTZ, no offset - the account runs one clock. Stated on every answer, survives turns once set. format: date-time is deliberately NOT used: it would reject this project's own timestamps.

binding_id.description: PATIENT_BINDING.binding_id. The human click that chose the subject. Null only for reference-corpus-only answers and CLASS_A refusals.

consent_id.description: The consent that authorised this answer, re-validated at query time on every tool call.

rule_versions.description: Every rule that contributed an outcome, with the version that decided it. Keyed by rule_id.

limitations.description: Explicit statements of what is not known or could not be verified. A stripped claim becomes a limitation here - never a silent removal.

allOf.description: A refused question cannot carry claims, and must name who may answer it. NMC TPG 2020 is a legal boundary, so the schema enforces it rather than the prompt.
A Class B answer is never 'refused'. Nothing found is a supported answer with a limitation and a timestamp.

text.description: Prose lives here and nowhere else.

outcome.description: Four-valued, never a boolean. not_evaluated is not fail.

provenance_note.description: Mandatory in the UI wherever a threshold is practice consensus rather than a guideline requirement. Carried here so the renderer cannot omit it.

action.description: What to do about a fail, not_evaluated or conflicting outcome, addressed to a named person or facility.

evidence.description: minItems 1 is the schema refusing an uncited claim. A claim with no evidence id must not be made.

structured.description: A governed row. Renders as the value, its three R2 clocks, the source facility, and the derivation if the number was computed rather than read.

derived.description: MANDATORY when the value was computed rather than read - ANC from a differential, CrCl from Cockcroft-Gault. JSON Schema cannot tell which, so validate_answer enforces it: a cited row carrying a derivation marker with no 'derived' string here strips the claim. Presenting a computed value as printed is a quiet form of fabrication.

document_span.description: DOC_PAGE plus char_start..char_end. Renders as the page with the span highlighted and a verification badge.

verification_status.description: R7. Never rendered as a percentage. 'conflicting' means the value is not asserted at all - such a span may appear as support for a limitation, never for a numeric claim.

reference_clause.description: A reference-corpus chunk. R6: rendered visually distinct from patient evidence, because a guideline clause in the same panel style as a pathology page invites reading it as a finding about the patient.

refusal.description: PROPOSED EXTENSION - see app/contracts/README.md. COPILOT-SPEC.md 2 shows only a Class B answer, so the frozen schema had no machine-readable home for the named practitioner that 4 promises in the refusal UI. Without this the Class A path cannot render its button.

practitioner.description: law-medical-records.md establishes adverse inference from record gaps. When the system says 'your treating team decides', it must name them.
